rows: Caveat: MMH 2947.70 (2 decimals) is −0.18 Å from Fe I 2947.8758, evidently a different MMH entry; Rowland 2947.99 − 0.106 ≈ 2947.88 agrees with Fe I. MMH gives only 2 decimals here and its value is 0.18 A shortward of Fe I 2947.876; MMH lists the feature as a blend (Fe II, Fe I, V II).
t — Fe I a5D3 - y5D*2 (blend with Fe I 2994.502 and Ni I 2994.453)
Rowland/Smithsonian: Fe; Wikipedia: Ni. MMH 1966 lists a blend dominated by Fe I with Ni I 2994.46 (NIST obs, 2 decimals) contributing.
T — Fe I a5D4 - y5D*4 (Rowland/Smithsonian T)
Conflict: Wikipedia T = Fe 302.108 nm, i.e. the multiplet partner Fe I 3021.0725 (MMH 3021.077, [30]).
S1/S2 — Fe I a5F4 - x5D*4 (blend with Fe I 3099.8943)
Smithsonian brackets S1, S2 over three Fe lines 3100.787/3100.430/3100.046 (Rowland scale).
P — Ti II a4F7/2 - z4G*9/2 (blend with Ti I/Sc II 3361.29)

Caveat: MMH 3361.193r lies 19 mÅ (−1.7 km/s) shortward of Ti II 3361.2121 — the solar feature is a blend (MMH: with 3361.287r). Rowland/Smithsonian attribute P to Fe; MMH 1966 and modern lists identify Ti II. Wikipedia's 336.112 nm does not match Ti II 336.121 nm or MMH 336.119 nm (apparent digit transposition).

Caveat: MMH 3441.019r is +30 mÅ above Fe I 3440.9885; MMH values below ≈3700 Å (r flags) are of historical quality (MMH − lab −1.7 to +2.7 km/s). Rowland O converts to the weaker 3441.0 line; the stronger multiplet partner Fe I 3440.6057 (MMH 3440.626r, EW 1243) is adjacent.
Strongest line in the visible solar spectrum (EW ~20 A).

NIST ASD gives only 3 decimals (no uncertainty) for Ca II H & K; Fraunhofer's H covered both H and K ('the two bands at H'). Core shows chromospheric H2V/H3 structure; H-epsilon (3970.07) lies in its wing.
unresolved fine-structure centroid (NIST blend row c58)

Rowland 4102.000 converts to ≈4101.85 Å (ISA), 0.10 Å redward of MMH 4101.748 — a historical Rowland-scale problem. Lab value = ASD level-less blend row c58, 4101.7346 +/- 0.0010 A (Ritz; gA-weighted centroid of the 7 components, reproduced as 4101.73463); ASD's n=2-6 multiplet line is Ritz 4101.7415 +/- 0.0024 A, 6.9 mA longer. IAG core fit pulled by Fe I 4101.68 blend. SCHOTT optics "h" = Hg 404.6561 nm.
Ritz: ASD level-less blend centroid (row c58)
SCHOTT optics "g" is instead Hg 435.8 nm.
NIST observed value is 4307.74 (2 decimals); Ritz 4307.744 used.
G — Fe I a3F3 - z3G*4 (in the CH G band)
Fraunhofer: 'At G there are massed together many lines' = the CH A-X (0,0) 'G band' 4290-4315 A plus Fe I/Ca I lines.
unresolved fine-structure centroid (NIST blend row c61)

Lab value = ASD level-less blend row c61, 4340.4634 +/- 0.0011 A (Ritz; gA-weighted centroid of the 7 components, reproduced as 4340.46344). ASD's n=2-5 multiplet line is Ritz 4340.471 +/- 0.003 A, 7.6 mA longer. Some lists (e.g. SEOS) call H-gamma 'f'.
Ritz: ASD level-less blend centroid (row c61)
d — Fe I a3F4 - z5G*5 (Rowland/Smithsonian d)
Designation conflict: Smithsonian/Rowland call Fe 4383.7 'd'; Wikipedia calls 438.355 nm 'e' and gives d = Fe 466.814 nm; D3 (He) is also called d.
d (Wikipedia) — Fe I z5D*2 - e5F3 (blend with Fe I 4668.061)
Only in modern lists (Wikipedia); a weak blended line (EW 112 mA) -- an odd choice for a lettered line. IAG fit affected by the blend.
unresolved fine-structure centroid (NIST blend row c64)

Lab value = ASD level-less blend row c64, 4861.3250 +/- 0.0014 A (Ritz): the gA-weighted centroid of the 7 components (reproduced as 4861.32497); components span 4861.2786-4861.3749 A. ASD's n=2-4 multiplet line, Ritz 4861.333 +/- 0.003 A (observed 4861.35 +/- 0.05 A, line ref. L7439c30), used in the airglow atomic table (Sect. 4), is 8 mA (0.49 km/s) longer. SCHOTT optics "F" = 486.1327 nm. HS5000 digitization 4861.35/EW 3000 disagrees with MMH page (4861.342m/3680).
Ritz: ASD level-less blend centroid (row c64)
Not in Fraunhofer's own list nor in the Smithsonian/Rowland table; found in modern lists (Wikipedia). Companion Fe I 4957.2983 (MMH 4957.307m) is in the same blend.
Rowland b3 = two lines (5169.220, 5169.069 Rowland) = Fe II 5169.028 + Fe I 5168.898. HS5000 gives EW 700 for 5168.91 (MMH page shows 114).
MMH value from OCR text layer, identical in HS5000 digitization (not checked on page image).
Fraunhofer's b: '3 very strong lines'. NIST gives no uncertainty for this Mg I value (4 decimals). HS5000 digitization has 5183.600 (error).
Caveat: MMH 5270.383 is a photographic blend centre (+17 mÅ vs APGL98 5270.3658; Ca I 5270.27 adjacent); not usable at the mÅ level. IAG fit not usable (core merges with Fe I 5270.356).
E1 — Fe I a3F2 - z3D*1 (blend with Ca I 5270.270)

Caveat: MMH 5270.383 is a photographic blend centre (+17 mÅ vs APGL98 5270.3658; Ca I 5270.27 adjacent); not usable at the mÅ level. Fraunhofer: 'E itself consists of several lines'. Smithsonian/Rowland E1 = Fe 5270.558 + Ca 5270.438 (Rowland scale) = Fe I 5270.356 + Ca I 5270.270; Wikipedia calls 527.039 nm 'E2' (it is Rowland's E1 Fe line).
e (optics) — Hg I 6s6p 3P*2 - 6s7s 3S1 (lamp line, not solar)
Glass-dispersion reference line borrowed the letter e. SCHOTT 2003 Table 9.1 gives 546.0740 nm; NIST ASD natural-Hg value 5460.750 A -- a 0.010 A difference (isotope composition / source).
D3 (or d) — He I 2p 3P - 3d 3D (main blend of 4 components)
solar chromosphere (emission at limb/prominences; not a disc-integrated absorption line)

NIST observed value is for the unresolved J=2->1,2,3 / 1->1,2 blend (no uncertainty given); Ritz components 5875.5987-5875.6404 A plus the weak 3P0-3D1 component at 5875.9663 A. gA-weighted centroid of all six components (derived, this work) = 5875.6610 A air. Discovered in the 1868 eclipse chromosphere (Janssen, Lockyer). SCHOTT optics "d" = 587.5618 nm (He lamp).
SCHOTT 2003: 587.5618 nm; defines n_d and the Abbe number V_d.
Caveat: solar Na D2 position is fit-dependent: MMH +22 mÅ, APGL98 flux +466 m/s, IAG core fit +816 m/s relative to lab; unresolved.
D — Na I D1+D2 doublet centre (arithmetic mean)

Derived row, not an observed line: the arithmetic mean of the NIST D1 and D2 values (air and vacuum); its uncertainty is the D1/D2 value 0.00003 A, taken as fully correlated (same source, L5918). Fraunhofer's original D (a pair). SCHOTT 2003 'D' = 589.2938 nm (centre of the double line); n_D is still quoted for glasses.
derived: mean of NIST D1 and D2
Fraunhofer's D was the pair. Interstellar/telluric Na can add narrow components in stellar spectra.
alpha (Greek) / Wikipedia a — O2 b-X (2,0): first line of the alpha group
O2 b      2 <- X      0; lower-state local quanta 'R 15Q 16     d'
MMH 1966 note: "First line of a group: 6276.590 A". Wikipedia 627.661 nm = mean of the MMH 6276.590/6276.633 blend. (HITRAN2020 wavenumbers are identical in HITRAN2024.)
alpha (Greek) — O2 b-X (2,0) gamma-band: chief line of the alpha group
O2 b      2 <- X      0; lower-state local quanta 'R  9Q 10     d'
6278.303 (double dagger: chief line in the alpha group)

Smithsonian/Rowland use Greek alpha for this O2 group; English & German Wikipedia list it as Latin 'a' (627.661 nm), conflicting with Fraunhofer's own a (between A and B). (HITRAN2020 wavenumbers are identical in HITRAN2024.)
SCHOTT 2003: 643.8469 nm (also the former primary length standard, red Cd line).
C — H I Balmer alpha (n=2-3), 7 fine-structure components
unresolved fine-structure centroid (NIST blend row c69)

Lab value = ASD level-less blend row c69, 6562.795 +/- 0.009 A (Ritz): the gA-weighted centroid of the 7 fine-structure components (reproduced by this work as 6562.79523). ASD also lists an n=2-3 multiplet line, Ritz 6562.819 +/- 0.007 A (observed 6562.79 +/- 0.03 A, line ref. L7400c29); the airglow atomic table (Sect. 4) uses that entry. The two composite values differ by 24 mA (1.1 km/s), more than either stated uncertainty: the difference comes from how the components are combined, not from a measurement. Components span 6562.7097-6562.9094 A (air); strongest 2p2P3/2-3d2D5/2 = 6562.85175 A. At 1e-3 A a Balmer line has no single wavelength. Neither composite is the geocoronal emission centre (2s-3p pair 6562.72483 / 6562.77153 A). SCHOTT optics "C" = 656.2725 nm. Solar core is chromospheric and asymmetric.
Ritz: ASD level-less blend centroid (row c69)
B — O2 b-X (1,0) B-band: first line of head
O2 b      1 <- X      0; lower-state local quanta 'R 21Q 22     d'

Caveat: the MMH blend pair 6869.887/6870.007 does not map cleanly onto HITRAN 6869.897/6869.974 (+32.6 mÅ for this pairing, larger than the +2–6 mÅ O₂ pressure shift). MMH 1966 note: "First line in head of B group: 6867.187 A" (Babcock & Herzberg 1948 O2 measurements). B is a band (6867-6967 A). (HITRAN2020 wavenumbers are identical in HITRAN2024.)
B — O2 b-X (1,0): Rowland's 'principal line in the head of B'
O2 b      1 <- X      0; lower-state local quanta 'R 11Q 12     d'
6870.182 (dagger: principal line in head of B)

Caveat: the MMH blend pair 6869.887/6870.007 does not map cleanly onto HITRAN 6869.897/6869.974 (+32.6 mÅ for this pairing, larger than the +2–6 mÅ O₂ pressure shift). Rowland value converted to ISA (~-0.21 A) matches the MMH 6869.887/6870.007 blend (HITRAN R13R13 6869.897 and R11Q12 6869.974 A air); the stronger HITRAN component is given. (HITRAN2020 wavenumbers are identical in HITRAN2024.)
a — H2O band group 0.72 um (telluric) -- Rowland reference line = solar Fe I
telluric band (Fraunhofer); solar Fe I (Rowland line)

Caveat: Fraunhofer's a is the telluric H2O band, and the solar values for this Fe I line are H2O-blended and disagree. MMH 7164.432 (disc centre) and the IAG core fit (-386 m/s) lie blueward of NIST Fe I 7164.4481, while the APGL98 flux value 7164.4578 is +406 m/s above it (+385 m/s above the Nave et al. 1994 value 7164.4486 used in APGL98b). Not a clean single-line reference. Fraunhofer (1817): "At a there are heaped together many lines which form a band" between A and B = telluric H2O bands (MMH 1966: H2O 400/301/202/221/103 bands, 6845-7480 A). Rowland/Smithsonian list a = 7164.725 (no element); MMH 1966 identifies the line at 7164.432 as solar Fe I (EW 153 mA). Strong telluric H2O lines lie within 0.1 A (HITRAN 7164.348, 7164.403 A air), so the solar position is blend-affected. Wikipedia/German WP "a = O2 627.661 nm" is the Greek-alpha O2 gamma-band group (Rowland alpha), a different feature.
627.661 (labelled a, O2; = Rowland/Smithsonian alpha group, see row alpha)
A — O2 b-X (0,0) A-band: R-branch head, line 2
O2 b      0 <- X      0; lower-state local quanta 'R 29Q 30     d'
Second component of the MMH 7593.695 band-head blend. (HITRAN2020 wavenumbers are identical in HITRAN2024.)
A — O2 b1Sg+ - X3Sg- (0,0) A-band: R-branch head, line 1
O2 b      0 <- X      0; lower-state local quanta 'R 27Q 28     d'

A is a BAND (O2 A-band, 7594-7684 A in MMH 1966), not a single line. Listed here: the band-head lines; MMH 7593.695 is the blend of the two HITRAN lines in rows A/A. Rowland gives two A lines: 7621.28 "beginning at the head of A, outside edge" and 7594.06 "single line beginning at the tail of A" (Rowland scale, ~+0.2 A vs ISA). Telluric: rest wavelength = lab; pressure shift delta_air ~ -0.005 to -0.010 cm-1/atm (= +3 to +6 mA at 1 atm). (HITRAN2020 wavenumbers are identical in HITRAN2024.)

Designation source is effectively Wikipedia; MMH supplies only the H₂O identification. Wikipedia lists Z as O2; MMH 1966 and HITRAN2020 identify the 8226.96 A line as H2O (no O2 transition in HITRAN within 500 cm-1). (HITRAN2020 wavenumbers are identical in HITRAN2024.)

Tentative identification: H₂O 8987.606 Å is 0.044 Å from the commonly quoted 898.765 nm; MMH does not cover this range. Wikipedia lists y = O2 898.765 nm; nearest strong HITRAN line is H2O at 8987.606 A (0.044 A away; S=5.8e-23). No O2 lines in HITRAN near 11123 cm-1. Identification tentative. (HITRAN2020 wavenumbers are identical in HITRAN2024.)
SCHOTT 2003: 1013.98 nm. NIST Ritz value used (10139.787 +/- 0.007 A air, 10142.567 A vac); the NIST observed value 10139.75 +/- 0.05 A is 7x less precise. (Solar t = Fe I 2994.4.)
